newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn and soybeans surge on dry weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn and soybeans surge on dry weather.

text.p: CBOT corn and soybean futures surged in fast trade amid forecasts for continued dry weather in parched portions of central Illinois, traders said.
Meteorologists said overnight weather maps indicated weekend rains would fall north of dry corn growing areas.
Some meteorologists also reduced chances for rain in Illinois early next week after Hurricane Danny began moving east instead of north.

The storm's quick surge to hurricane status surprised meteorologists, causing some to change their forecasts. Weather Express Inc's Fred Gesser, who on Thursday expected the storm to push rain into the Midwest, said Friday the Hurricane's path will keep rain out of the Midwest.

Persistent hot, dry weather can damage corn and soybean crops and cut yield potential. Heat and moisture stress are of concern to corn as the crop enters the critical pollination period, traders said.
At 0942 CDT, soybeans were up 10-3/4 to 8-1/2 cents per bushel with November up 8-3/4 at $6.09-1/2. Corn was up 5-3/4 to 4-3/4 cents per bushel with December up five at $2.53-1/2.
